claim: Legionella pneumophila is the causative agent of Legionnaires' disease
source: The causative agent of Legionnaires' disease, Legionella pneumophila, delivers more than 330 virulent effectors to its host to establish an intracellular membrane-bound organelle called the Legionella containing vacuole.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature establishing this relationship

claim: Legionella pneumophila delivers more than 330 virulent effectors to its host
source: The causative agent of Legionnaires' disease, Legionella pneumophila, delivers more than 330 virulent effectors to its host to establish an intracellular membrane-bound organelle called the Legionella containing vacuole.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the number of effectors, supported by established knowledge in the field

claim: Legionella pneumophila establishes an intracellular membrane-bound organelle called the Legionella containing vacuole
source: The causative agent of Legionnaires' disease, Legionella pneumophila, delivers more than 330 virulent effectors to its host to establish an intracellular membrane-bound organelle called the Legionella containing vacuole.

claim: SidC and its paralog SdcA have been identified as novel bacterial ubiquitin E3 ligases
source: Among the army of Legionella effectors, SidC and its paralog SdcA have been identified as novel bacterial ubiquitin (Ub) E3 ligases.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior research establishing the E3 ligase activity of these proteins

claim: The crystal structure of a binary complex of the N-terminal catalytic SNL domain of SdcA with its cognate E2 UbcH5C was determined
source: To gain insight into the molecular mechanism of SidC/SdcA as Ub ligases, we determined the crystal structures of a binary complex of the N-terminal catalytic SNL domain of SdcA with its cognate E2 UbcH5C and a ternary complex consisting of the SNL domain of SidC with the Ub-linked E2 UbcH7.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript

claim: The crystal structure of a ternary complex consisting of the SNL domain of SidC with the Ub-linked E2 UbcH7 was determined
source: To gain insight into the molecular mechanism of SidC/SdcA as Ub ligases, we determined the crystal structures of a binary complex of the N-terminal catalytic SNL domain of SdcA with its cognate E2 UbcH5C and a ternary complex consisting of the SNL domain of SidC with the Ub-linked E2 UbcH7.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript

claim: The two structures reveal the molecular determinants governing the Ub transfer cascade catalyzed by SidC
source: These two structures reveal the molecular determinants governing the Ub transfer cascade catalyzed by SidC.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural data presented in the study

claim: The donor Ub is immobilized with its C-terminal tail locked in an extended conformation during the Ub transfer cascade
source: Together, our data support a common mechanism in the Ub transfer cascade in which the donor Ub is immobilized with its C-terminal tail locked in an extended conformation, priming the donor Ub for catalysis.
evidence: This is a mechanistic conclusion supported by structural observations in the study

claim: Legionella pneumophila is an intracellular opportunistic human pathogen
source: Legionella pneumophila is an intracellular opportunistic human pathogen that causes a severe form of pneumonia termed Legionnaires' disease (Cunha et al., 2016; Rowbotham, 1980).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations

claim: Legionella pneumophila causes a severe form of pneumonia termed Legionnaires' disease

evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations

claim: Legionella uses a Dot/Icm type IV secretion system to secrete over 330 effector proteins into the host cytosol following phagocytic uptake
source: Following phagocytic uptake, Legionella uses a Dot/Icm (Defective organelle trafficking/Intracellular multiplication) type IV secretion system to secrete over 330 effector proteins into the host cytosol (Ensminger, 2016; Qiu and Luo, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Legionella infection mechanism, supported by citations

claim: The concerted action of Legionella effectors leads to the formation of the LCV
source: The concerted action of these effectors leads to the formation of the LCV (Legionella-containing vacuole), an organelle that prevents lysosome-mediated degradation of the invading bacteria while also serving as a replicative niche (Isberg et al., 2009; Swanson and Isberg, 1995; Tilney et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations

evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations

claim: The LCV serves as a replicative niche for Legionella

claim: The biological functions of most Legionella effectors are as yet unknown
source: Although the biological functions of most Legionella effectors are as yet unknown, a number of effectors have been shown to modulate a rather diverse array of host cellular processes, including membrane trafficking, cellular signaling, lipid metabolism, and in particular, the host ubiquitination pathway (Hubber et al., 2013; Hubber and Roy, 2010; Lin and Machner, 2017; Qiu and Luo, 2017).

claim: Ub is covalently attached to substrates in a three-enzyme cascade

claim: Ub is first activated by an E1 activating enzyme, then transferred to one of approximately 30 E2 conjugating enzymes, and finally ligated to a substrate by one of hundreds of E3 Ub ligases
source: Ub is first activated by an E1 activating enzyme, then transferred to one of approximately 30 E2 conjugating enzymes, and finally ligated to a substrate by one of hundreds of E3 Ub ligases.

claim: E3 ligases can be divided into three major classes: RING E3s, RBR E3s, and HECT E3s
source: The E3 ligases, which play a crucial role in the ubiquitination cascade, can be divided into three major classes: Really Interesting New Gene (RING) E3s (Deshaies and Joazeiro, 2009), Ring-Between-Ring (RBR) E3s (Aguilera et al., 2000), and Homologous to E6AP C-terminus (HECT) E3s (Huibregtse et al., 1995; Rotin and Kumar, 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations

claim: Each of the three classes of E3s uses a distinct strategy to transfer Ub
source: Each of the three classes of E3s uses a distinct strategy to transfer Ub (Berndsen and Wolberger, 2014).

claim: RING E3s promote a 'closed conformation' of the E2~Ub by locking the C-terminus of Ub into the active site groove on the E2 to facilitate direct Ub transfer from the E2~Ub to a substrate
source: The RING E3s promote a 'closed conformation' of the E2~Ub by locking the C-terminus of Ub into the active site groove on the E2 to facilitate direct Ub transfer from the E2~Ub to a substrate (Dou et al., 2012; Plechanovová et al., 2012; Pruneda et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about RING E3 mechanism, supported by citations

claim: HECT E3s catalyze a transthiolation reaction that transfers Ub from E2~Ub to the E3 catalytic cysteine residue
source: The HECT E3s catalyze two distinct reactions: a transthiolation reaction, which transfers Ub from E2~Ub to the E3 catalytic cysteine residue; and a subsequent aminolysis reaction, which transfers Ub from E3~Ub to a substrate lysine (Huibregtse et al., 1995).
evidence: This is established knowledge about HECT E3 mechanism, supported by citation

claim: HECT E3s catalyze an aminolysis reaction that transfers Ub from E3~Ub to a substrate lysine
source: The HECT E3s catalyze two distinct reactions: a transthiolation reaction, which transfers Ub from E2~Ub to the E3 catalytic cysteine residue; and a subsequent aminolysis reaction, which transfers Ub from E3~Ub to a substrate lysine (Huibregtse et al., 1995).

claim: RBR family E3 ligases share features of both RING and HECT E3s and utilize a hybrid mechanism for Ub transfer
source: The third class, the RBR family of E3 ligases, shares features of both RING and HECT E3s and utilizes a hybrid mechanism for Ub transfer (Dove et al., 2016; Wenzel et al., 2011).
